narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Detect a current ordered-plan entry whose lifecycle entity is already terminal

## Context

Consumer bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI on Directive 0.109.1: issue 287 completed its product and lifecycle PRs, but .deft/plan-sequence.json still recorded issue 287 as the pending current entry. The behavior remains present in Directive 0.110.0 and master commit 212481b98051e9988f0a15748400c6afc154b2a5.

## Expected behavior

A deterministic read-only verifier should report when the current ordered-plan entry resolves to a completed, failed, or cancelled lifecycle entity while the plan entry remains non-terminal, and require explicit operator-reviewed reconciliation. Completed history must not automatically select or authorize the next target.

## Actual behavior / gap

scope:complete and swarm cohort closeout update lifecycle state without advancing the ordered plan. verify:plan-sequence only checks whether a requested target matches the current entry, so the cross-ledger contradiction passes and the separate plan-sequence:advance step can be omitted.

## Session notes

Minimal reproduction: create an ordered plan with issue A current; complete and land A through scope:complete; omit plan-sequence:advance; verify:plan-sequence still accepts A although its lifecycle entity is terminal. Acceptance should add a side-effect-free terminal-entry drift finding, preserve explicit operator authority for advancement, and provide one remediation. Related broad umbrellas: deftai/directive issues 3913 and 3910; neither explicitly covers this exact state.

---

Unknown policy reuses orphan-active `StateResolution` or stays filesystem-only so unknown does not arise.

Drift predicate: current plan entry is non-terminal (`status` pending or unset, sequence not exhausted) and a resolvable Directive lifecycle origin for that entry already sits in `completed/` or `cancelled/` (or carries the failed stamp). GitHub `closed` without a terminal xBRIEF stays on #3429 / #3476.

Fail-closed surfaces: `plan-sequence:current` (work selection) and `verifyPlanTarget` (work-unit plus sub-agent admission). Solo `swarm:launch` skip and dummy-target cohort admission are in that surface list, or they are a named leftover; they are not closed by editing only `packages/cli/src/verify-plan-sequence.ts`.
Printed remediation is operator-reviewed stop/ask, same voice as orphan-active's do-not-complete-until, not unattended `plan-sequence:advance`.
New result code, not `mismatch` or `exhausted`, so agents cannot treat drift as pick-the-next-id.
Share one pure drift helper between `plan-sequence:current` and `verifyPlanTarget`. Do not add a third verb.

## Gate stamp

The triage author stamps the semantic call. Round-1 ceiling is this write-back (N=1).

P1 is that `verify:plan-sequence` compares only whether a requested target matches `entries[current_index]`. `scope:complete` and swarm closeout can make that current entry's issue/PR terminal without advancing the sequence. The cross-ledger contradiction passes, and the next authorized target stays the completed work.

What this P1 is not:

- Not `verify:orphan-active` (active xBRIEFs whose issues are closed).
- Not #4433 `batching_allowed` (parallel-wave authorization).
- Not automatic advance. Completed history must not select the next target.
- Not GitHub-only status as the sole ledger. The ordered-plan file is the authorization record.

Re-measured at `eda261d7a6e0d75b61466c6234ea517cd77df598`: `packages/cli/src/verify-plan-sequence.ts` calls `verifyPlanTarget` only. No terminal-lifecycle drift finding exists in that path.

Open critique of #4129 at dispatch SHA `eda261d7a6e0d75b61466c6234ea517cd77df598`. Input ceiling 5746684311 (Stop 1 write-back). No later comments read.

Re-verified at that SHA, not from line cites:

- `verifyPlanTarget` (`packages/core/src/plan-sequence/types.ts`) returns ok on kind+id match of `entries[current_index]`. Its body contains none of `status`, `completed`, `cancelled`, `failed`, `lifecycle`, `xbrief`, `github`, `orphan`.
- `packages/cli/src/verify-plan-sequence.ts` calls that function only. No sequence → exit 0 skip. Match → exit 0. It requires `--target-kind` and `--target`; there is no current-entry scan.
- `git grep plan-sequence` on `packages/core/src/scope/main.ts`, `lifecycle-write.ts`, `swarm/complete-cohort.ts`, and `swarm/finalize-cohort.ts` is empty. `scope:complete` / cohort closeout do not advance `.deft/plan-sequence.json`.
- `admitSwarmLaunchPlanSequence` (`packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts`) calls `verifyPlanTarget(seq, { targetKind: "story", target: "swarm-cohort" })` only when `dispatchKind === "swarm-cohort"`. Solo launch skips it. `allocationPlanId` plus `batchingRationale` bypasses a rejected admission.
- Existing terminal vocabulary already lives on xBRIEF lifecycle: `TIP_TERMINAL_FOLDERS = completed | cancelled` (`packages/core/src/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts`); `hasTransitionWrite` / failed `plan.status` (`packages/core/src/scope/lifecycle-write.ts`); origin extraction `collectGithubRefs` (`packages/core/src/orphan-active/refs.ts`); unknown-state policy `StateResolution` live|inventory|cache|unverified (`packages/core/src/orphan-active/issue-state.ts`).

Stop 1 P1 (match-only `verify:plan-sequence` still authorizes a current entry whose lifecycle is already terminal; advance can be omitted) is true as far as it goes. It is not yet a bindable bound remedy.

## 1. Lifecycle resolution, ledger, and unknown policy are unbound

blocks-the-design

Evidence: `PlanSequenceEntry.kind` is `pr | issue | story | task | phase | checklist | review`, with optional `issue` and `title`. GitHub issue state is `open | closed` only. The issue's expected tokens are `completed, failed, or cancelled`, which already name xBRIEF folders and the failed stamp, not forge state. Stop 1 says GitHub-only status is not the sole ledger, without saying whether GitHub is necessary, sufficient, optional corroboration, or out of scope. `verifyPlanTarget` is a pure function; orphan-active already owns unverified/skip-gh/cache-age.

Failure mode: an implementer following Stop 1's file pointer adds a GitHub `state===closed` read inside `verify:plan-sequence` or `verifyPlanTarget`. Then either (a) unverified/outage fail-opens and today's hole remains whenever `gh` is down, (b) unverified fail-closes every ordered-plan work unit on forge outage, (c) `kind=story` swarm entries with no `issue` field never resolve and silently stay authorized, or (d) GitHub-closed is treated as sufficient terminal and recuts `lifecycle-write.ts` ("GitHub-closed is not authority to mint complete") plus `verify:completed-tracked` (closed forge issue still needs a tracked completed/cancelled blob).

Disposition consequence: the successor map cannot bind until it names (1) the resolution function from a plan entry to a lifecycle entity per kind, including "no origin" (skip vs fail), (2) which existing ledgers are sufficient for terminal — inventory first: `TIP_TERMINAL_FOLDERS` + `hasTransitionWrite` + `collectGithubRefs` on the current entry's origin, not a new issue-state client — and (3) the unknown policy, either by reusing orphan-active `StateResolution` or by staying filesystem-only so unknown does not arise.

## 2. P1's "authorized next target" is not the CLI match path, and the one remediation must not auto-advance

blocks-the-design

Evidence: preamble §2.55 binds "what's next?" to `plan-sequence:current` and requires `verify:plan-sequence` only before a new work unit (PR, branch, story activation, sub-agent). `plan-sequence:current` prints the current id and exits 0 whenever the sequence is not exhausted; it does not call `verifyPlanTarget`. `resolveContinuation` in this module has no CLI caller (queue's same-named helper is a different function). `advancePlanSequence` is the write that marks current `completed` and moves `current_index`, which is what authorizes the next entry. Sibling verifiers print `run task …` remediations (`orphan-active/evaluate.ts`, `completed-tracked-on-delivery.ts`). Solo `swarm:launch` never calls `verify:plan-sequence` or `verifyPlanTarget`. Cohort admission uses dummy target `swarm-cohort`, not the launched story ids.

Failure mode: a bound remedy that only adds a drift finding to `packages/cli/src/verify-plan-sequence.ts` (Stop 1's re-measurement) leaves `plan-sequence:current` still naming issue 287 as next, and leaves solo swarm dispatch still launching that story. Completed work remains the authorized next target on the work-selection and sub-agent paths. Separately, if the one remediation is `task plan-sequence:advance`, agents follow printed `run task` lines unattended and the next entry becomes authorized without operator review — the auto-advance the issue forbids.

Disposition consequence: bind must list the fail-closed surfaces (at least `plan-sequence:current` for work selection and `verifyPlanTarget` for work-unit plus sub-agent admission, or an explicit leftover that swarm/solo stay out). The printed remediation must be operator-reviewed stop/ask, in the same voice as orphan-active's "Do not run task scope:complete until …", not an unattended advance. A new result code (not `mismatch` / `exhausted`) is required so agents cannot treat drift as "pick the next id". Dummy-target cohort admission and the solo skip are in that surface list, or they are a named leftover; they are not closed by editing the CLI file Stop 1 pointed at. `#4433` `batching_allowed` stays out (unused persist-only field; Stop 1 already excluded it).

## 3. Reuse the xBRIEF terminal folders; do not invent a forge-state lifecycle entity

sharpens-framing

Evidence: consumer reproduction is issue 287 after product and lifecycle PRs, which is exactly a tracked origin under `xbrief/completed/` (or cancelled/failed). `evaluateCompletedTracked` already pairs closed GitHub issues with those folders; `verify:orphan-active` already pairs closed GitHub issues with leftover `active/` briefs. Stop 1 correctly says this P1 is not orphan-active.

Failure mode: specifying "GitHub closed" as the lifecycle entity duplicates those two gates, imports their unverified policy, and still misses story-kind entries whose terminal evidence is a completed xBRIEF basename rather than `issue.state`.

Disposition consequence: state the drift predicate as: current plan entry is non-terminal (`status` pending or unset, sequence not exhausted) and a resolvable Directive lifecycle origin for that entry already sits in `completed/` or `cancelled/` (or carries the failed stamp). GitHub `closed` without a terminal xBRIEF stays on `#3429` / `#3476`. That is a wording change, not a second verifier.

## Injection / swarm lens

The target changes who may start the next ordered-plan unit versus who already finished a lifecycle entity. GitHub issue/PR bodies and `state` are untrusted. Using forge-closed to *advance* would let a close on the current issue authorize the next entry; the issue correctly forbids that. Using forge-closed to *fail-closed* current is a stall, not an injection into next, but outage/unverified then reconstitutes today's hole or blocks all ordered-plan work. `plan-sequence.json` is shared authorization across dests; dest-local `scope:complete` can terminal an xBRIEF in one worktree while primary `current_index` still points at it, and the reverse. `plan-sequence:advance` is not occupancy-gated, so any agent can currently write the next authorization. Swarm identity: solo launch skips the only machine gate; cohort checks a dummy story id; explicit allocation-plan consent bypasses rejection. A CLI-only finding does not sit on those paths.

## Road not taken

Auto-advance on detection — rejected; it makes lifecycle (including untrusted forge state) select the next authorized target. A new GitHub issue-state reader inside `verifyPlanTarget` — rejected in favor of the existing local terminal folders unless the successor map explicitly takes leftover unknown-policy from orphan-active. A third verb beside `verify:plan-sequence` — unnecessary if `verifyPlanTarget` plus `plan-sequence:current` share one pure drift helper; a CLI-only add is the measured miss above.

## Steelman

CLI-only fail-closed on match is enough because preamble already requires `verify:plan-sequence` before a new work unit, so agents stop on 287 and must ask. What would flip that: a path that treats `plan-sequence:current` as authorization without the CLI, which is the measured solo `swarm:launch` path and the `current` verb itself.

GitHub-closed as the lifecycle entity matches the consumer's wording ("issue 287 completed"). What would flip that: the expected tokens `completed | failed | cancelled` already naming xBRIEF lifecycle, and `lifecycle-write.ts` already refusing GitHub-closed as complete-authority.

## Footnotes

footnote `entry.status` is parsed (`pending | completed | skipped`) and ignored by `verifyPlanTarget`. `advancePlanSequence` pairs status with index except when `exhausted` (already fail-closed). Hand-edit only; not the consumer bug (status stays pending).

footnote `#3913` / `#3910` are open lifecycle-authority epics and do not specify this cross-ledger predicate. No `4129` xBRIEF exists at this SHA.

footnote vitest was not executed here (`npx` 401 against the registry). Re-verification is `git show` / `git grep` at `eda261d7a6e0d75b61466c6234ea517cd77df598`.
